result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.trophic_incoherence_parameter()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Measure how far a directed network is from a perfect trophic hierarchy. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L37070-L37141){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.trophic_incoherence_parameter( weighted=None, cannibalism=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Trophic incoherence parameter](/assets/graphs/trophic-incoherence-parameter.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The food web of grass, rabbit, mouse, fox and owl, laid out by trophic level with each edge labelled by its level difference: four edges of exactly 1, mouse to owl 1.5 and fox to owl 0.5. The card takes their mean, 1.0, and their standard deviation, q = 0.29; a perfectly layered web would score 0." width="100%"} The trophic incoherence parameter `q` (Johnson et al., 2014) is the standard deviation of the trophic differences over all edges (see `trophic_differences()`). A perfectly layered network, where every edge climbs exactly one level, has `q = 0`; higher values mean edges skip levels or loop back. Trophic coherence predicts stability in food webs and appears in gene regulation, neural and other directed networks: coherent networks tend to have few cycles and to be more stable. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether trophic levels weight diets by edge weight. If `None` (default), follows the graph. [cannibalism]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `False` (default), self-loops are removed before computing levels and differences, as in NetworkX. If `True`, they are kept. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The trophic incoherence parameter `q` (population standard deviation). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : As for `trophic_levels()`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A food chain is perfectly coherent; adding an omnivore link that skips a level makes it less so: ::: {#a1f48275 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec chain = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["plant", "herbivore", "carnivore"]) chain.add_edges([("plant", "herbivore"), ("herbivore", "carnivore")]) coherent = chain.trophic_incoherence_parameter() chain.add_edge("plant", "carnivore") coherent, round(chain.trophic_incoherence_parameter(), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.0, 0.408) ``` ::: :::
